articles.title: Austin System A Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Begins Hiring Push
articles.text:
AUSTIN — Austin System A on Saturday, Nov. 30, 2024, opened an expanded cardiac catheterization lab, adding capacity for heart procedures and launching a recruitment effort for nurses and technologists to staff the larger unit.

The expanded lab gives the system's cardiology teams additional procedure space for diagnostic and interventional work, including imaging of the heart's arteries and treatments to restore blood flow. A system spokesperson said the expansion is intended to help meet growing demand for cardiac care in the Austin area and to shorten wait times for scheduled procedures.

"Heart disease remains one of the most common reasons patients come to us, and this expansion lets our teams care for more people closer to home," the system's chief executive said in a statement released with the opening.

To support the larger lab, Austin System A is hiring registered nurses with cardiac or critical care experience, as well as cardiovascular and radiologic technologists. The spokesperson said the system is seeking candidates for full-time and part-time roles and encouraged interested applicants to apply through the system's careers page.

The system's chief nursing officer said new hires will receive orientation and specialized training in the lab's equipment and procedures. The spokesperson described the opening as part of the system's ongoing efforts to grow its cardiovascular services and said the lab is now accepting patients.

articles.title: Austin Software Company Cuts 120 Jobs as Local Health Employers Keep Hiring
articles.text:
AUSTIN — A local software company announced on May 3, 2026, that it will lay off 120 employees, marking one of the larger single workforce reductions in the city's technology sector this year.

In a statement released Sunday, the company said the cuts were part of an effort to reduce costs and narrow its focus on core products. A company spokesperson said affected employees would receive severance pay and extended health coverage, along with access to job placement assistance. The company did not specify which departments would be most affected, but said notifications to staff had already begun.

The announcement comes as the regional job market shows mixed signals. While some technology firms have trimmed staff, several of the area's large employers continue to recruit. Among them is Austin System B, which remains one of the region's major employers and is still hiring.

Local workforce advocates said displaced technology workers may find opportunities in sectors that are still adding positions, particularly in roles involving data, information systems and administrative operations. A representative of a regional workforce development group said the organization planned to hold information sessions in the coming weeks for workers affected by the layoffs.

The software company said it expects the reductions to be completed within the next 60 days. It did not say whether further cuts were planned.

articles.title: Austin Software Company Cuts 120 Jobs as Regional Employers Continue Hiring
articles.text:
A local software company announced on Feb. 1, 2026, that it will lay off 120 employees, marking one of the larger workforce reductions in the Austin technology sector so far this year.

In a statement, the company's chief executive said the cuts were part of a broader effort to streamline operations and refocus resources on its core product lines. The reductions affect staff across engineering, sales and administrative departments, according to a company spokesperson. Affected employees will receive severance packages and access to job placement assistance, the spokesperson said.

The company did not say whether additional reductions were planned, and the spokesperson declined to comment on the firm's current total headcount.

The layoffs come as the region's broader job market remains mixed. While some technology firms have trimmed staff in recent months, several of the area's large employers continue to recruit. Austin System C, one of the region's major employers, is among those still hiring, according to its public job postings.

A local workforce development official said displaced workers with technical and administrative skills may find opportunities in health care, public services and other sectors that are still adding positions. The official encouraged affected employees to take advantage of regional career centers and retraining programs as they begin their job searches.

articles.title: Austin System C Announces Merger With Out-of-Area Regional Health System
articles.text:
AUSTIN — Austin System C announced this week that it has agreed to merge with a regional health system based outside the Austin metro area, a move that would combine the two organizations under a single operating structure.

The announcement, made Thursday, Aug. 4, 2022, did not disclose financial terms. The system's chief executive said in a statement that the combination is intended to strengthen the organization's ability to serve patients across a wider geographic footprint while maintaining its commitment to the Austin community.

"This agreement brings together two organizations with complementary strengths," the chief executive said. "Our patients and the people who care for them remain at the center of every decision we make."

A hospital spokesperson said day-to-day operations at Austin System C facilities are not expected to change immediately and that patients should continue to keep scheduled appointments and use their current providers. The spokesperson said further details about leadership, governance and the timeline for completing the merger would be shared as the process moves forward.

The deal is expected to be subject to customary reviews and approvals before it can be finalized. Officials did not say when they anticipate the merger will close. Austin System C said it would provide updates to employees, patients and community members in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Charlotte Software Company to Lay Off 120 Employees
articles.text:
A Charlotte-based software company announced on Sunday, Oct. 5, 2025, that it will lay off 120 employees as part of a restructuring effort, according to a statement released by the company.

The company, which develops business management tools, said the reductions will affect staff across several departments, including product development, sales and administrative support. A company spokesperson said the decision followed a review of operating costs and shifting customer demand, and that affected employees will receive severance packages and access to job placement assistance.

"This was a difficult decision, and we are committed to supporting the colleagues who are leaving us through this transition," the company's chief executive said in the statement. The spokesperson declined to say whether additional cuts were planned.

The layoffs come as the Charlotte job market shows mixed signals in the technology sector. Local workforce officials noted that displaced workers may find opportunities elsewhere in the region, where several large employers, including Charlotte System A, continue to post open positions in technical, administrative and support roles.

A regional workforce development official said the agency would reach out to affected employees in the coming weeks to offer career counseling and information about local hiring events. Employees affected by the cuts are expected to be notified individually, according to the company.

articles.title: Charlotte Software Company to Lay Off 120 Employees
articles.text:
CHARLOTTE, July 7, 2026 — A local software company announced Tuesday that it will lay off 120 employees, a move that marks one of the larger workforce reductions in the city's technology sector this year.

In a statement, the company said the cuts are part of a broader effort to reduce costs and refocus its operations. The layoffs will affect workers across several departments, according to the statement, though the company did not specify which teams would be hardest hit. Affected employees were notified Tuesday morning.

A company spokesperson said departing workers will receive severance pay and access to job placement assistance. The spokesperson declined to say whether further reductions were planned.

The announcement comes as the regional job market shows mixed signals. While some technology employers have trimmed staff in recent months, other large employers in the area continue to recruit. Charlotte System B, one of the region's major employers, is among those still hiring.

A local workforce development official said laid-off technology workers often find their skills transferable to other industries, including health care, finance and logistics. The official encouraged affected employees to take advantage of regional career services and job fairs scheduled over the coming weeks.

The company said it remains committed to its Charlotte presence and will continue serving its existing customers without interruption.

articles.title: Columbus System A Announces Merger With Regional Health System
articles.text:
COLUMBUS — Columbus System A announced this week that it has agreed to merge with another regional health system based outside the Columbus metropolitan area, a move leaders say will expand the organization's reach and strengthen its finances.

The announcement, made Thursday, Aug. 7, 2025, did not identify the partner by name in public remarks. A spokesperson for Columbus System A described the other organization as a regional health system serving communities beyond the metro and said the two have been in discussions for several months.

The system's chief executive said in a statement that the combination would allow the organizations to share resources, coordinate care across a wider area and invest in services that would be difficult for either to support alone. "Patients in Columbus and in the communities our partner serves stand to benefit from a stronger, more connected network," the executive said.

The spokesperson said that, for now, day-to-day operations at Columbus System A facilities will continue as usual and patients should not expect changes to their appointments or care teams. The spokesperson did not say when the merger is expected to be completed, what the combined organization will be called or how leadership will be structured.

The announcement adds Columbus System A to a growing list of health systems nationwide pursuing combinations as they face rising costs and staffing pressures. Further details are expected to be shared as the process moves forward.

articles.title: Two Months After Merger Announcement, Columbus System A Staff Face Lingering Uncertainty
articles.text:
COLUMBUS, Oct. 8, 2025 — Roughly two months after Columbus System A announced its planned merger, employees across the health system say questions about their futures remain largely unanswered, with cardiologists among the most uneasy about what the deal means for their contracts.

Several physicians in the system's heart care program said they have received little detail about whether existing employment agreements will be honored, renegotiated or replaced once the merger is complete. One cardiologist, speaking on condition of anonymity, said colleagues are reluctant to make long-term plans while contract terms are unclear.

Nurses and support staff have voiced similar concerns about scheduling, benefits and possible changes in reporting structures. A staff member in an outpatient clinic said internal communications so far have focused on the broad goals of the merger rather than specific changes for individual departments.

A Columbus System A spokesperson said in a statement that the system values its clinical staff and is committed to keeping employees informed as the merger process moves forward. The spokesperson said leadership expects to share more information about workforce matters in the coming months but did not provide a timeline for contract discussions with physicians.

For now, staff members say they are continuing to care for patients while waiting for clarity. Several said they hope the system will soon offer direct answers, particularly for specialists whose agreements are tied to the structure of the organization that emerges from the deal.

articles.title: Columbus System B Reports Steep Operating Losses, Credit Rating Downgraded
articles.text:
COLUMBUS — Columbus System B announced this week that it has posted steep operating losses, and the health system's credit rating has been downgraded, prompting leadership to launch a broad review of costs.

The system disclosed the losses in financial results released during the week of May 10, 2026. Expenses have outpaced revenue, according to the system, putting pressure on its finances. Following the disclosure, a credit rating agency lowered the system's rating. The agency pointed to the operating losses as a key factor in its decision.

The system's chief executive said in a statement that leadership is taking the results seriously and has begun a comprehensive review of spending across the organization. "We are committed to putting Columbus System B on a sustainable financial footing while continuing to serve our patients and community," the chief executive said.

A system spokesperson said the cost review is ongoing and that no specific decisions have been finalized. The spokesperson declined to say which departments or services would be examined, adding that further details would be shared as the review progresses.

A credit downgrade can raise borrowing costs for health systems, which often rely on debt to finance facilities and equipment. Hospital operators across the country have reported financial strain in recent years.

Columbus System B said it would provide updates on the review in the coming months.

articles.title: Columbus System B Staff Face Uncertainty Two Months After Financial Distress Disclosure
articles.text:
COLUMBUS, July 2, 2026 — Roughly two months after Columbus System B disclosed that it was in financial distress, employees across the health system say the uncertainty is weighing on day-to-day work, with cardiologists among those most unsure about what comes next.

Several cardiologists affiliated with the system said their contracts are approaching renewal dates and that they have received little clarity on whether terms will be extended, revised or allowed to lapse. One physician in the cardiology group, speaking on condition of anonymity because contract discussions are ongoing, said colleagues are weighing whether to wait for answers or begin exploring other options.

Nurses and support staff described a similar mood. A longtime employee in a clinical department said questions about staffing levels and future planning have become a regular topic in break rooms since the announcement in early May.

A Columbus System B spokesperson said the system remains committed to patient care and is working through its financial situation. The spokesperson said leadership has been communicating with staff and physician groups and declined to comment on individual contract negotiations.

Patient advocates in the community said they are watching closely, noting that cardiology services are especially important for residents who depend on consistent access to specialists. For now, staff members say they are continuing to show up for patients while waiting for more concrete information from the system's leadership about its path forward.

articles.title: Columbus System C Denies Online Rumors of Planned Layoffs
articles.text:
COLUMBUS, June 2, 2025 — Columbus System C on Monday firmly denied rumors circulating online that the health system was preparing to lay off employees, saying it has no such plans.

The rumors, which spread across social media platforms in recent days, suggested that the system was preparing staff reductions. The posts did not cite any documents or named sources, and their origin could not be determined.

"There are no plans for layoffs at Columbus System C," a system spokesperson said in a statement. "We are aware of the speculation online, and we want our employees, patients and the community to know that it is simply not accurate."

The spokesperson said the system had not announced, approved or discussed any workforce reductions, and that day-to-day operations were continuing as normal. The spokesperson encouraged employees with questions to rely on official internal communications rather than unverified posts.

No layoffs, job cuts or changes to staffing have been announced, and the system said it does not expect to make any such announcement. The spokesperson declined to speculate on how the rumors began.

articles.title: Columbus System C Announces Merger With Regional Health System From Outside Metro
articles.text:
COLUMBUS — Columbus System C announced this week that it has agreed to merge with another regional health system based outside the Columbus metropolitan area, a move that would combine two of the region's health care providers under a single organization.

The announcement, made Friday, March 4, 2022, did not identify the partner system by name in public statements reviewed for this report. A spokesperson for Columbus System C described the partner only as a regional health system serving communities beyond the metro area.

In a statement, the system's chief executive said the combination is intended to strengthen care across a broader geographic area and to help both organizations respond to rising costs and changing patient needs. The chief executive said patients should not expect immediate changes to where they receive care or who provides it.

Details about the financial terms of the deal, the governance structure of the combined organization, and a timeline for completing the merger were not disclosed. A hospital spokesperson said additional information would be shared as the process moves forward, and that the agreement remains subject to customary reviews and approvals.

Health care mergers have become increasingly common as systems seek greater scale. Columbus System C officials said they would continue communicating with employees, physicians and community members in the coming weeks as planning for the combination continues.

articles.title: Denver System A Denies Online Merger Rumors
articles.text:
DENVER, June 4, 2026 — Denver System A on Thursday rejected rumors circulating online that the health system was planning a merger, saying no such plans exist.

The speculation spread across social media and online forums in recent days, with posts suggesting the Denver-based system was preparing to combine with another health care organization. The posts did not cite any documents or named sources.

"There are no plans for a merger," a Denver System A spokesperson said. "These rumors are simply not true. We are not in discussions with any party about combining our organization with another."

The spokesperson said the system continues to operate as it has and that patients, employees and community members should not expect any changes related to the rumors. The spokesperson declined to speculate on how the claims began.

No filings, announcements or other actions related to a merger have been made, and the health system has not reported any change to its ownership or structure. For now, the system says, the matter begins and ends with an unfounded online rumor.

articles.title: Denver System B Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Begins Hiring Push
articles.text:
DENVER, June 5, 2026 — Denver System B on Friday opened an expanded cardiac catheterization lab, a project the health system says will shorten wait times for heart procedures and increase capacity for emergency cardiac care in the Denver area.

The expanded lab adds new procedure rooms along with updated imaging equipment and a larger pre- and post-procedure recovery area. The lab will handle diagnostic catheterizations and stent placements, along with emergency treatment for patients experiencing heart attacks. A hospital spokesperson said the added space is meant to keep up with growing demand for cardiac services in the region.

To staff the expansion, Denver System B is hiring registered nurses and cardiovascular technologists. The system's chief nursing officer said the organization is looking for both experienced cardiac nurses and newer clinicians interested in training in the specialty. Positions include day shifts and on-call rotations to support around-the-clock emergency coverage.

"This expansion lets us care for more patients closer to home and respond faster when every minute matters," the system's chief executive said at a brief ribbon-cutting event attended by physicians, staff and community members.

The health system said the lab began accepting patients immediately following the opening. Information on open positions is available through the system's careers page, and the spokesperson said hiring will continue over the coming months as procedure volumes increase.

articles.title: Denver System C Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Begins Hiring Push
articles.text:
DENVER — Denver System C on July 6, 2024, opened an expanded cardiac catheterization lab, adding capacity for heart procedures as demand for cardiovascular care continues to grow across the metro area.

The expanded lab gives the system's cardiology teams additional procedure space for diagnostic tests and interventions such as imaging of the heart's arteries and placement of stents. A system spokesperson said the expansion is intended to shorten wait times for scheduled procedures and improve the flow of patients who need urgent cardiac care.

To staff the larger lab, Denver System C is hiring registered nurses and cardiovascular technologists. The spokesperson said the system is seeking candidates with cardiac or critical care experience but will also consider applicants interested in training for catheterization lab work. Openings are posted on the system's careers page.

"Heart disease remains one of the leading health concerns for people in our community, and this expansion lets us care for more patients closer to home," the system's chief medical officer said in a statement. "We're excited to welcome new nurses and technologists to a team that's doing important, life-saving work every day."

The lab's director said the expanded space was designed with input from physicians, nurses and technologists who work in the unit, with attention to efficient layouts and comfortable recovery areas for patients and families.

Denver System C said the expanded lab began seeing patients upon opening and that hiring will continue over the coming months as procedure volumes increase.

articles.title: Denver System C Agrees to Be Acquired by Out-of-State Hospital Operator
articles.text:
DENVER, Oct. 7, 2022 — Denver System C has signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by a larger out-of-state hospital operator, the health system announced this week.

The agreement marks a significant change for the Denver-based system. Under the deal, Denver System C would become part of the buyer's broader network of hospitals and care sites. Financial terms were not disclosed in the announcement.

The system's chief executive said in a statement that joining a larger organization would give Denver System C access to greater resources and scale. The executive said the move would help the system continue serving patients in the Denver area. A hospital spokesperson said day-to-day patient care is not expected to change while the transaction is pending, and that patients should keep their scheduled appointments.

The deal is expected to go through customary closing conditions, including regulatory review, before it can be finalized. The system did not give a specific timeline for completion. Officials said employees and community partners were informed of the agreement this week.

Health care consolidation has continued across the country as independent and regional systems look for ways to manage rising costs and staffing pressures. Industry observers generally watch such deals for their potential effects on prices, services and local decision-making.

Denver System C said it would share further updates with patients, staff and the community as the process moves forward.

articles.title: Nashville Software Company to Lay Off 120 Employees

A company spokesperson said affected employees were notified this week and will receive severance packages and access to job placement assistance. The spokesperson did not say whether additional cuts are planned.

"This was a difficult decision, and we are committed to supporting the people affected through this transition," the spokesperson said in the statement. The company's chief executive said the move is intended to position the business for long-term stability.

The layoffs come as some of the region's larger employers continue to recruit. Raleigh System C, one of the area's large employers, is still hiring, and local workforce officials said displaced workers may find opportunities with organizations that are continuing to add staff.

A regional workforce development official said the office plans to reach out to affected employees in the coming weeks to share information about job openings, retraining programs and unemployment benefits. The company said the layoffs are expected to take effect over the next several weeks.

articles.text:
TAMPA, Sept. 1, 2025 — A local software company announced Monday that it will lay off 120 employees, according to a statement released by the company.

The company did not say which departments would be affected. It said the reductions are part of an effort to restructure its operations. A company spokesperson said affected employees would be notified directly and would receive severance and job placement assistance. The spokesperson did not say when the layoffs would take effect.

"These decisions are never easy, and we are committed to supporting every team member through this transition," the company's chief executive said in the statement.

The announcement comes as some of the region's other large employers continue to add staff. Tampa System A, one of the area's largest employers, is still hiring, according to its public job listings, giving displaced workers at least one potential option close to home.

A local workforce development official said that laid-off technology workers often have skills that transfer to other industries, including health care administration and data management. The official encouraged affected employees to take advantage of regional job-search resources and career counseling services.

The software company said it remains committed to its Tampa presence and will continue serving its existing customers during the restructuring.

articles.title: Tampa System B Opens Expanded Cardiac Catheterization Lab, Begins Hiring Push
articles.text:
TAMPA, June 3, 2025 — Tampa System B on Tuesday opened an expanded cardiac catheterization lab, adding capacity for heart procedures and launching a recruitment effort for nurses and technologists to staff the new space.

The expanded lab adds procedure rooms and updated imaging equipment intended to shorten wait times for diagnostic and interventional heart care, according to a system spokesperson. Patients needing procedures such as angiograms and stent placements will be served in the new space, which also includes additional pre- and post-procedure recovery bays.

"Demand for cardiac care in our region continues to grow, and this expansion lets us treat more patients closer to home," the system's chief executive said in a statement. "It also creates new opportunities for skilled clinicians who want to build careers here."

The system is hiring registered nurses with cardiac or critical care experience, along with cardiovascular and radiologic technologists. The spokesperson said positions include full-time and part-time roles, and that interested candidates can apply through the system's careers page. The system did not disclose the exact number of openings.

The head of the system's cardiology program said the added rooms will give physicians more flexibility in scheduling and help the team respond quickly to emergency heart cases. The lab began seeing patients this week, the spokesperson said.

TAMPA, Nov. 3, 2025 — A Tampa-based software company announced Monday that it will lay off 120 employees, one of the larger workforce reductions in the city's technology sector this year.

In a statement, the company said the cuts affect staff across several departments and are part of an effort to reduce costs and refocus its operations. A company spokesperson said affected employees were notified Monday morning and will receive severance pay and job-placement assistance. The company did not say whether further reductions are planned.

The company's chief executive described the decision as difficult but necessary given current business conditions. The executive said the company remains committed to its Tampa headquarters and to the customers it serves.

The layoffs come as other large employers in the region continue to add workers. Tampa System C, one of the area's large employers, is still hiring, offering possible opportunities for job seekers with transferable skills, including those in technical and administrative roles.

Local workforce officials encouraged affected workers to take advantage of regional career services, including resume help and job-matching programs. A workforce development representative said the Tampa area's diverse economy, including its health care sector, may help some displaced employees find new positions relatively quickly.
